title: Auto-brief: incident transfer insights with playbook & cost links
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: design an ‘auto-brief’ surface that appears during incident/on-call transfer and from alert details. The auto-brief synthesizes the most important signals for fast decisions: alert origin, recent SLO delta(s), approximate incremental cost delta (tokens/estimated GPU time), linked playbook fragments, and one-click postmortem or escalation actions.

Why: current handoff workflows require responders to hunt across alert, SLO dashboards, cost views, and playbooks. We want a compact, machine-assisted TL;DR to reduce time-to-ack and ensure runbooks are followed.

Scope: prototype the compact surface, handoff flow where the brief is pinned to the incident timeline, and a lightweight authoring affordance so runbook authors can mark playbook fragments that surface in the brief. Include desktop and mobile breakpoints. Create hi-fi Figma screens for review and an accessibility pass (contrast, keyboard focus).
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after workshop with SRE and Support. Captured pain points: ambiguous alert origins, missing SLO snapshots during handoff, and 'who pays' uncertainty for burst capacity. Proposed compact brief with three zones: (1) snapshot (SLO delta + alert origin), (2) impact (cost estimate + affected customers), (3) actions (playbook links + quick actions).

2026-03-11 Alex Rivera: Rough wireframes uploaded to Figma. Added a 'pin brief to timeline' interaction and 'flag for postmortem' checkbox. Asked ENG to confirm available signals for cost estimation (per-request token counts & runtime meta).

2026-03-12 Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed PRD. Requested a 2-step fallthrough for missing runbook fragments (suggested auto-search + author notification). Also asked to add 'privacy-safe' flags when incident includes customer PII. Added label request for security review if PII appears.

2026-03-13 Jon Kim (SRE): Engineering comment - we can expose SLO delta and token counters via runtime telemetry endpoint. Cost estimate accuracy depends on batch window; suggested showing a range (low/median/high) and last-sampled timestamp. Added ENG-98765 as dependency for telemetry contract.

2026-03-14 UX critique session notes: participants (Design, PM, SRE, Support). Outcomes: simplify language on the brief, replace 'cost' with 'estimated compute cost' tooltip, make playbook fragments editable inline, and surface a 'confidence' score for automated excerpts. Action: iterate hi-fi mocks and prepare accessibility checklist.
review_feedback: PM review (Priya Nair): Approve direction; request for acceptance criteria and success metrics added.
Eng review (Jon Kim): Accept with dependency on telemetry contract; flagged performance risk for pinning briefs to many timeline entries.
Design review (Luca Moretti): Minor UI tweaks: reduce icon density, improve affordance for 'assign' button on mobile.
acceptance_criteria: Compact brief renders in alert details and can be pinned to an incident timeline entry.

Brief includes: alert origin, SLO snapshot (current and delta), estimated compute cost (range) with timestamp, linked playbook fragments, and primary quick actions (Acknowledge, Assign, Flag for Postmortem).
Design provides hi-fi Figma screens for desktop and mobile and a downloadable spec PDF.
Authoring flow demonstrated: runbook fragment tagging UI and suggested auto-excerpt behavior with confidence score.
Usability test: average time-to-comprehension for responders decreases by at least 30% in lab tasks vs baseline (benchmarked in PRD).
Accessibility: color contrast and keyboard navigation pass automated checks; screen reader labels included for each action.
